definitions.explanation: The main or central railway station in a city, typically the largest or most important station serving as the primary hub for train services. Used both as a general term and as part of specific station names.

examples.japanese: {中央駅|ちゅうおうえき}で{降|お}りてください。
examples.english: Please get off at the central station.

examples.japanese: {中央駅|ちゅうおうえき}の{改札|かいさつ}{口|ぐち}で{待|ま}ち{合|あ}わせた。
examples.english: We arranged to meet at the ticket gate of the central station.

examples.japanese: ヨーロッパの{都市|とし}には「{中央駅|ちゅうおうえき}」と{名付|なづ}けられた{大|おお}きな{駅|えき}があることが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many European cities have large stations named 'Central Station.'

notes:
Composed of {中央|ちゅうおう} (center, central) and {駅|えき} (station). While Japan does not typically name stations this way (preferring city-name-based naming like {東京駅|とうきょうえき}), the term is commonly encountered when discussing foreign train stations or as a general descriptor. Some Japanese cities do have stations with {中央|ちゅうおう} in the name, such as {千葉中央駅|ちばちゅうおうえき}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {中央駅|ちゅうおうえき}{前|まえ}: in front of the central station
- {中央駅|ちゅうおうえき}から{徒歩|とほ}で: on foot from the central station
- {中央駅|ちゅうおうえき}{周辺|しゅうへん}: the area around the central station

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {主要駅|しゅようえき}: main station — emphasizes importance rather than location
- {終着駅|しゅうちゃくえき}: terminal station — the last stop on a line
- {乗換駅|のりかええき}: transfer station — a station for changing lines
